title: rules the model only follows become checks a script makes
description: Tasks, one rule per task, each deleting its prose: (1) audit-task start refuses a task that is not ready unless --force, which journals the exception. (2) Phase status and claim are written by a verb, not a hand edit. (3) executor.runsGate is resolved by a script, not by the model reading config. Measure the mandatory-read bytes of /audit:next before and after each. Waits for the pipeline pilot in the measurement phase.
desiredOutcome: the first rules the orchestrator prose asks the model to follow are made by scripts instead, each with a test and with its prose section deleted, and the bytes an execution command must read go down with each move

tasks.title: audit-task start refuses a task that is not ready unless --force, which journals the exception
tasks.description: start reports what a task waits on but never refuses ('REPORTED, NEVER REFUSED' in _locked_start), so readiness is a rule the model only follows. Make start refuse a pending task with unmet references, unless --force with --reason, which the task.start row journals. It reads _status_facts.unmet_refs, with no second copy of the rule. Starting a task by hand for the plan gate keeps working through --force. Delete the prose the rule came from: the term list and the 'Satisfied' paragraph under orchestrator.md's '## Readiness rule'. Keep the heading, which _areas.py and _priority.py cite, and keep the priority and parallel-safety paragraphs. Point commands/next.md step 1 at the ready list and the refusal, document the flags in commands/task.md, and move README.md's Readiness row from the 'Followed' table to the enforced one. Record `wc -c` of commands/next.md and the reference files it requires, before and after. This phase waits for P101's pipeline pilot (P101.1), whose findings decide which prose rules move first.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py: start on a pending task whose dependsOn, own blockedBy or phase blockedBy is unmet refuses, names each unmet reference as _status_facts.unmet_refs spells it, and writes nothing
plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py: start --force --reason on the same task starts it, and its task.start row records the forced exception with the reason and the unmet references
plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py: start on a ready task, and a re-start of an in_progress task (the retry path), behave as before (allow cases)

outcome.technical:
audit-task.py start now refuses a task whose own or phase references are unmet, unless the task is already in_progress (a retry). The check goes through _waiting_on, which reads _status_facts.unmet_refs, so the readiness rule exists in one place. The refusal exits 2, writes nothing, adds no journal row, names each unmet reference as /audit:status spells it (e.g. `P2 (phase)`), and points to --force --reason. New --force flag; VERB_FLAGS["start"] = ("force", "reason"); _start_flags_refusal refuses --force without --reason and --reason without --force; --reason - reads stdin. A forced start writes mode: forced, reason and basis ("unmet: ...") on its task.start row (keys already in _journal_io.DETAILS_KEYS); its summary says FORCED past unmet ...; --json gains forced and forcedReason. An ordinary start writes none of these.
Decisions: a blocked task with unmet references is refused too (the rule is about unmet references, not the status label); --force on a task that is already ready is accepted and records nothing extra.
Docs: orchestrator.md's Readiness rule keeps its heading, priority and parallel-safety paragraphs; the term list and 'Satisfied' paragraph are replaced by a pointer to ready_tasks, unmet_refs and the start refusal. next.md step 1 takes the first READY NOW entry. task.md: argument hint, a --force example, the journal bullet, the refusal list, and the readiness paragraph. README: the Readiness row moves from Followed to the enforced table; the /audit:task row names --force. test__refs.py pf2 lists start among verbs whose hint carries flags (scope widened for exactly that).
Bytes (wc -c), this task's share: next.md 2453 -> 2456, orchestrator.md 57593 -> 57353.
Tests: test_audit_task pr10, pr10b, pr10c, pr11, pr11b replace the old report-only pr10/pr11; pr11c is the allow twin (a ready task starts with no mode on its row; a re-start of an in_progress task is not refused). Red-first proved through the helper at HEAD b6d9a4a3: 715/720 with exactly pr10-pr11b failing. Suites: test_audit_task 720/720, test__refs 304/304, test__areas, test__output, test__deps, test__priority green; ruff clean.
outcome.descriptive: audit-task start now refuses a task that is not ready unless it is forced with a recorded reason, so readiness is enforced by the script instead of being a rule the model reads and follows.

intentCheck.basis: orchestrator check: the refusal reads unmet_refs, writes nothing on refusal, a forced start records mode, reason and basis, the readiness term list left orchestrator.md, and red-first was proved with allow twins

tasks.title: audit-task start writes the phase claim, and the hand-edited phase-entry steps are deleted
tasks.description: execute-task.md's step 1a tells the model to Edit phase.status to in_progress, which start already does through _panel_write's phase promotion. Step 1d tells it to hand-write phase.claim into the shard. Make start write the claim on the sharded layout; sign-off already releases it. Then delete the prose the rule came from: steps 1a and 1d under execute-task.md's '## Execute the task'. Keep the 1b-1c pointer to the verb, and keep README.md's '§ Execute the task 1b–1c' citation pointing at the step that remains. Record the mandatory-read bytes of /audit:next before and after. Like the rest of this phase, it waits for P101's pipeline pilot.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py: start of a sharded plan's first task writes phase.claim {sessionId from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, host, branch, at} into the shard in the same write that sets phase.status in_progress, and the task.start row records it
plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py: start on a single-file plan writes no claim, and a re-start by the claiming session leaves the claim as it was (allow cases)
plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py: start on a phase another session has claimed names that claim and refuses unless --force, which replaces it and journals the claim it replaced

outcome.technical:
audit-task start now writes phase.claim on the sharded layout, in the same _write_add that _heal_phase_status promotes the phase in: {sessionId from $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID (read through _journal_io.ENV_SESSION_VAR), branch (entry or current), at}. No host is written: the shard is committed, and the journal drops actor.host for the same reason. _claim_plan decides before any write (none / keep / take / contested / no-session). A claim held by another session is refused with exit 2 before any write, naming that claim's session, branch and at; --force --reason replaces it and journals the claim it replaced (forced gains replaced). The task.start row carries phase-keyed changes rows for claim.sessionId, claim.branch and claim.at; --json gains claim, claimAction and claimReplaced. With no session id, no claim is written and the output says so. Any start on a sharded phase with no claim takes one (re-entry after an interruption included); a re-start by the holding session keeps the claim byte for byte.
execute-task.md: steps 1a (hand-edit phase.status) and 1d (hand-write phase.claim) are deleted; step 1 says the start verb sets both and refuses another session's claim; the b-c sub-step keeps its label because README and _invariants cite it. /audit:next's mandatory-read bytes (wc -c of next.md, orchestrator.md, manifest-conventions.md, execute-task.md): 151841 -> 151193.
No host anywhere: _manifest_vocab.CLAIM_KEYS = (sessionId, branch), so a claim the verb writes revalidates with no warning; _manifest_phases' wording follows; the schema's claim description says host stays an accepted key (COMPATIBILITY.md) but the plugin writes none; gen-demo-manifest's lease has the same shape (no committed render moved: check-rendered-artifacts --before-commit OK); tools/check-committed-pii.py reports plan-claim-host for a host under any phase claim in a committed plan file; prove-gates' schema_subset_drift row re-anchored on the new CLAIM_KEYS.
Docs: task.md (argument hint, claim bullet, journal rows, refusal list, --force and --json keys), README's /audit:task row.
Tests: test_audit_task pc1-pc8 (pc3 the allow twin; pc7 no host key; pc8 a started sharded plan revalidates with no claim warning while a branchless claim still warns); check-committed-pii q32 plus q24/q25 fixtures (a host-free claim stays clean); test__manifest_phases mp10/mp11, test__manifest_vocab mv25/mv27/mv28, test_gen_demo_manifest lease cases updated to derive from CLAIM_KEYS. Red-first proved through the helper at HEAD 775df9c1 (pc1, pc2, pc4, pc5, pc6; 721/726); pc7 and pc8 were red in the shared tree before their fixes; the PII cases were proved by never-fire and over-fire mutations (33/36 each). Full sweep 305/305 files ok; prove-gates --selftest 37/37; validator OK.
outcome.descriptive: Starting a task now records which session holds the phase - without naming the machine, since the plan is committed - and refuses a phase another session holds unless forced with a recorded reason, so the two hand-edit steps the orchestrator used to follow are gone.

intentCheck.basis: orchestrator check: the claim is written by the verb in the same write as the phase promotion, steps 1a/1d deleted with bytes measured, and the orchestrator's privacy correction (no host, PII backstop) applied across verb, validator, schema text, demo and check

tasks.title: the spawn brief resolves executor.runsGate, and the orchestrator no longer reads config for it
tasks.description: execute-task.md step 3 tells the model to read .claude/audit.config.json through hooks/_config.load() and executor_gate_policy(), and to state the reading in the spawn prompt. Instead, audit-lookup.py brief, whose answer is already pasted into that prompt, resolves it and prints the word with its basis. It calls executor_gate_policy loaded through _loader, the way _gate_feed does, because a script may not import hooks/. An unrecognised value is a refusal, not the default. Delete the prose the rule came from: the bullet 'Resolve executor.runsGate the same way — at spawn, by you' in execute-task.md step 3. The brief bullet carries the line instead. Update audit-lookup's PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md section and regenerate the module map. Record the mandatory-read bytes of /audit:next before and after. It waits for P101's pipeline pilot.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_lookup.py: brief --project on a project whose config sets executor.runsGate to full prints that reading with the key as its basis, in text and in --json
plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_lookup.py: with the key or the config file absent, brief prints own-tests and says it is the default
plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_lookup.py: an unrecognised runsGate value makes brief exit non-zero, naming the value and printing no reading, never the default

outcome.technical: audit-lookup.py brief now resolves executor.runsGate itself and prints it as the brief's last line with its basis (set by executor.runsGate in .claude/audit.config.json; or the default, with no config file or with the key unset), and adds it to --json as runsGate {reading, default, basis}. It reads hooks/_config.executor_gate_policy through _loader the way _gate_feed does, on the project's config as written, so an absent key is told apart from one set to the default. An unrecognised value, or a config that does not parse, is refused on stderr with exit 3 and no reading, rather than defaulted. execute-task.md step 3's bullet telling the orchestrator to resolve executor.runsGate itself is deleted; the brief bullet says its last line is the reading to paste and to stop and ask the human when brief refuses. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md's audit-lookup section and the module-map line are updated. Mandatory reads of /audit:next measured with `git cat-file -s HEAD:<file>` against `wc -c`: execute-task.md 57795 to 56398 bytes, the four files together 153475 to 152078. Cases rg1-rg7 in test_audit_lookup.py; red-first proved through the helper (40/47 at HEAD); mutations (an invalid value folded into the default, the keyed flag forced false, every set value refused) each reddened their cases.
outcome.descriptive: The brief the orchestrator pastes into an executor's prompt now states how the executor's own gate is to run, read from the project's config by a script, so the orchestrator no longer has to read the config and follow instructions to do it.

intentCheck.basis: orchestrator check: the brief prints the reading with its basis and refuses an unknown value, the prose step is deleted, and the bytes measurement is recorded; red-first proved
